# Guild

> **Origin:** Guild was originally derived from
> [Strata](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata) by Niko1221 and contributors,
> then substantially reworked as an independent Mixture-of-Experts inference engine.

**Guild is a native C++ inference runtime focused on high-performance local execution of Mixture-of-Experts models.**

Guild is especially designed for asymmetric systems that conventional GPU-centric runtimes may underuse, such as servers with large amounts of system RAM, powerful CPUs, and limited GPU VRAM.

## Why Guild?

Large Mixture-of-Experts models do not need every parameter for every token.

Guild is designed around that fact.

It can distribute model execution across:

- GPU VRAM
- system RAM
- CPU compute
- storage-backed expert tiers

while dynamically planning KV cache placement, expert residency, speculative decoding, and other runtime resources around the hardware actually available.

Guild is particularly useful on systems such as:

- large-RAM servers with modest GPUs
- dual-socket and NUMA systems
- consumer GPUs paired with large system memory
- older GPUs with limited VRAM
- heterogeneous or otherwise asymmetric machines

## Current status

Guild is under active development.

Core remains v0.x. See [version and revision policy](docs/releases/VERSIONING.md)
and [build/release pipelines](docs/releases/PIPELINES.md) for build identity,
development artifacts and release validation gates.

Current work includes:

- native C++ model loading and inference
- architecture-independent model descriptors
- Mixture-of-Experts expert scheduling
- GPU / RAM / file expert tiering
- native execution memory planning
- host-only KV cache support
- speculative / MTP decoding
- native OpenAI-compatible HTTP serving
- native model registry and downloader
- persistent in-process model execution
- hardware telemetry and benchmarking

### Architecture support

| Architecture | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Qwen3.8 / qwen4exp | Supported / primary development target |
| Qwen3.5 MoE / Ornith | Experimental / active development |
| GLM MoE | Planned |
| DeepSeek-style MoE | Planned |
| Mixtral-style MoE | Planned |
| Other architectures | Experimental as added |

Support status may change quickly while Guild is under active development.

## Quick start

Guild currently builds from source.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/guild-inference/Guild.git
cd Guild

cmake -S . -B build \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DGUILD_ENABLE_CUDA=ON

cmake --build build -j$(nproc)
```

Then:

```bash
./build/guild --help
```

The long-term installation path will be a native installer and prebuilt releases.

## Commands

```text
guild pull <model>       Download a model
guild import <path>      Import an existing local model
guild list               List installed models
guild show <model>       Inspect a model
guild run <model>        Run a model interactively
guild serve <model>      Start the OpenAI-compatible server
guild bench <model>      Benchmark a model
guild ps                 Show running model processes
```

Some commands and options are still evolving.

## Serving

Guild includes a native OpenAI-compatible HTTP server.

Example:

```bash
guild serve <model>
```

By default, Guild should bind locally.

Typical endpoint:

```text
http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1
```

Supported API functionality is still evolving.

## Performance philosophy

Guild is not intended to be a generic wrapper around every model architecture.

Its primary goal is to extract high performance from sparse and Mixture-of-Experts models, especially on hardware where:

- system RAM is much larger than VRAM
- memory placement matters
- expert routing can be exploited
- CPU and GPU resources can work together
- conventional all-GPU execution is impractical

Performance claims should be based on reproducible benchmarks using equivalent model formats and settings.

## GPACK and GEXEC

Guild is developing two native model formats:

**GPACK**

A portable Guild model package containing model weights, architecture metadata, tokenizer assets, auxiliary models such as MTP components, and other hardware-independent information required to run the model.

**GEXEC**

A machine-optimized execution artifact produced from a GPACK.

A GEXEC may contain hardware-specific choices such as:

- tensor layouts
- kernel selections
- expert packing
- NUMA placement
- KV strategy
- speculative decoding configuration
- hardware-specific tuning results

GPACK is portable.

GEXEC is optimized for a specific execution environment.

Both formats are still under development and should not yet be considered stable.

## Project philosophy

Guild aims to remain:

- local-first
- open source
- native C++
- MoE-focused
- transparent about memory placement and execution
- usable without a required cloud service or account

Python bindings may be provided separately, but Python is not intended to be required by the Guild runtime.

## Contributing

Guild is young and changing quickly.

Bug reports, hardware results, architecture work, kernel optimizations, documentation improvements, and compatibility testing are welcome.

Please include relevant hardware details when reporting performance or runtime issues.

Start with [docs/CONTRIBUTING.md](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) for the build, test and formatting commands, and
[docs/architecture/README.md](docs/architecture/README.md) for the component map and the per-subsystem documents.

## Security

Please report security vulnerabilities privately using GitHub's private vulnerability reporting feature.

See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

## Support

Guild is developed and tested on personally owned hardware.

Contributions can help fund:

- additional GPUs
- larger memory configurations
- storage for large model testing
- compatibility testing
- model validation

The original Strata copyright and license notices are preserved as required.

# Architecture Guild runs a mixture-of-experts model on one normal PC: one GPU (NVIDIA or AMD) plus system RAM, on Windows or Linux. The engine is C++ (CUDA or HIP kernels); a Python layer in `serve/` provides the web app and the Anthropic-shaped API in front of the engine's OpenAI-compatible server. This file is the map. It says what the parts are, how a token flows through them, and which document has the detail - it repeats none of them. ## The three layers, and the one rule | Layer | Lives in | Owns | | --- | --- | --- | | **Core / orchestration** | `src/runtime`, `src/core`, `src/memory`, `src/plan`, `src/prefill`, `src/spec`, `src/artifact`, `src/abi`, `src/server`, `src/cli`, `src/models` | Loading, the memory plan, the layer and token loops, speculative decoding, containers, packages, HTTP, CLI, the model store | | **Model runners** | `include/guild/model/runner.hpp`, `src/model/` | Per-architecture mapping of container metadata and tensors to a `ModelDescriptor`, the required operations, the geometry and capability checks | | **Hardware kernels** | `src/kernels`, `src/core/*.cu`, `plugins/`, `sycl/` | The arithmetic: the CPU expert pool (AVX2 / AVX-512 / NEON), CUDA dense, attention and MoE, HIP, plus external providers | The rule that keeps them decoupled: **resolution happens once, off the hot path**. Core asks the `KernelRegistry` for one implementation per operation while the model loads, keeps the resulting function pointers and package ids, and then calls them directly. Inside a token or layer loop there is no virtual dispatch and no registry lookup - see [MODULAR_RUNTIME.md](MODULAR_RUNTIME.md#execution-lifecycle--zero-overhead-hot-path) for why that is a hard rule and not a preference. The layers meet at two contracts: * the C ABI in `include/guild/abi/` (`kernel_abi.h`, `cpu_expert_abi.h`, runner and lifecycle headers) - plain values, explicit error info, no C++ types across the boundary; * the `.gkmetadata` / `.gkernel` / `.gkmodule` package format, which is how a provider that was not compiled into this binary gets loaded, verified and leased ([KERNEL_ABI.md](KERNEL_ABI.md), [GKERNEL_FORMAT.md](GKERNEL_FORMAT.md), [GKMODULE.md](GKMODULE.md)). A consequence worth knowing: the same Core builds a CPU-only engine, a CUDA engine and (experimental) a SYCL engine, and which kernels exist is a build-time and load-time question, not a set of `#ifdef`s in the loops. ## Component map ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph clients["Clients"] oai["HTTP clients
OpenAI / Anthropic wire formats"] web["serve/
web app, MCP tools, Jinja chat templates"] cli["guild CLI"] end subgraph core["Core"] srv["src/server
HTTP listener, SSE streaming
src/runtime
GuildModel / GuildSession"] plan["src/memory
memory planner"] loops["src/core, src/prefill, src/spec
layer loop, batched prefill, verifier, drafters"] reg["src/kernels/registry.cpp
operation registry + leases"] pkg["src/abi
package manager, trust, install"] end subgraph providers["Providers"] cpu["CPU expert pool
+ native CPU arithmetic"] cuda["CUDA dense / attention / MoE"] hip["HIP backend"] ext["external .gkernel / .gkmodule"] end oai --> srv web -->|subprocess, line protocol| srv cli --> srv cli --> loops srv --> loops plan --> loops loops --> reg pkg --> reg reg --> cpu reg --> cuda reg --> hip reg --> ext ``` ## Artifacts: what a model is on disk ```mermaid flowchart LR gguf["GGUF shards"] -->|guild convert| gpack["GPACK .gpack
portable: tensors, metadata,
tokenizer, expert blob"] gpack -->|guild optimize| gexec["GEXEC .gexec
tuned for one host"] gpack --> run["guild run / bench / serve"] gexec --> run ``` * **GGUF** is the import format, and remains a valid one: the runtime can load shards directly. * **GPACK** ([GPACK_FORMAT.md](GPACK_FORMAT.md)) is the portable container: one memory-mapped file with the tensor index, dense weights, optional embedded expert blob, tokenizer assets and auxiliary models. The mapping *is* the model - weights are views, not copies. * **GEXEC** ([GEXEC_CONTRACT.md](GEXEC_CONTRACT.md)) is not a model: it is what this machine measured about running that model (kernel selection, expert layout, placement plan, workspace sizes), pinned to a hardware and ABI fingerprint. An artifact that does not match is ignored with a reason, never used approximately. ## Memory hierarchy The planner (`src/memory/planner.cpp`) places everything, and every tier below exists because VRAM is the scarce resource; [CPU_GPU_WORKLOAD_ANALYSIS.md](../performance/CPU_GPU_WORKLOAD_ANALYSIS.md) has the measurements that drove the split. | Tier | Holds | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Device VRAM | Dense weights, KV/attention state, expert cache slots, scratch | Sized by the plan, finalised against live free VRAM at load | | Pinned host RAM | RAM-resident expert complement, host KV tier | Locked pages for fast H2D; NUMA interleaved when locked pages do not fit | | Mapped file | Experts the tiers above do not take | Zero-copy out of the GPACK; the page cache does the caching | | Peer GPU | A second expert tier | Bit-identical expert rows, same kernels as the primary's hit path | ## Where to read next | Document | Scope | | --- | --- | | [EXECUTION_LIFECYCLE.md](EXECUTION_LIFECYCLE.md) | Startup stages, session creation, prefill, the decode/speculative window, ownership and failure rules | | [MODULAR_RUNTIME.md](MODULAR_RUNTIME.md) | The three layers in detail, phase status, the hot-path rule | | [MODEL_RUNNERS.md](MODEL_RUNNERS.md) | What a runner is, how one is resolved from metadata, how to add one | | [KERNEL_ABI.md](KERNEL_ABI.md), [GKERNEL_FORMAT.md](GKERNEL_FORMAT.md), [GKMODULE.md](GKMODULE.md) | The C ABI, `.gkernel` packages, runtime `.gkmodule` components | | [GPACK_FORMAT.md](GPACK_FORMAT.md), [GEXEC_CONTRACT.md](GEXEC_CONTRACT.md) | Container layouts, identity and invalidation rules | | [CPU_BACKEND_OWNERSHIP.md](CPU_BACKEND_OWNERSHIP.md), [CUDA_BACKEND_OWNERSHIP.md](CUDA_BACKEND_OWNERSHIP.md), [EXTERNAL_BACKENDS.md](EXTERNAL_BACKENDS.md), [REPOSITORY_SPLIT_PLAN.md](REPOSITORY_SPLIT_PLAN.md) | Which repository owns which arithmetic, and the gates between them | | [PHASE2E_CONCURRENCY.md](PHASE2E_CONCURRENCY.md), [PHASE2E_PACKAGE_LIFECYCLE.md](PHASE2E_PACKAGE_LIFECYCLE.md) | Session/package concurrency and package lifetimes | | [../quality/CODE_STYLE.md](../quality/CODE_STYLE.md), [../CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) | How to write and build code here | | [../performance/](../performance/), [../performance/PHASE6_LONG_CONTEXT_OPTIMIZATION.md](../performance/PHASE6_LONG_CONTEXT_OPTIMIZATION.md), [../performance/PHASE65_GENERAL_OPTIMIZATION.md](../performance/PHASE65_GENERAL_OPTIMIZATION.md), [../performance/PHASE66_ADAPTIVE_SPECULATIVE_DECODING.md](../performance/PHASE66_ADAPTIVE_SPECULATIVE_DECODING.md), [../quality/](../quality/), `bench/results/` | Measurements, populated long-context curves, adaptive speculative decoding benchmarks, `llama.cpp` reference comparisons, and audits - every number with the machine it was measured on |

# Execution lifecycle This document follows one process from `guild run` to a generated token: what happens at load, what a session is, how a request is served, and which invariants hold across all of it. It is the narrative counterpart to [MODULAR_RUNTIME.md](MODULAR_RUNTIME.md) (which explains the layering rule) and to the headers it cites (which state each contract in full). The order below is the order in the code. `GuildModel::load` in `src/runtime/model.cpp` performs exactly these stages, and each stage is also a field of `StartupProfile`, so the startup JSON that a run prints is a timeline in this order. ## 1. Startup: `GuildModel::load` ```mermaid flowchart TB a["Device runtime policy"] --> b["Enabled .gkmetadata packages
load_enabled_packages"] b --> c{"Container?"} c -->|"explicit .gpack"| d[".gpack opens or the load fails"] c -->|"GGUF shards"| e["shards open"] d --> f["Runner resolution
architecture + capability checks"] e --> f f --> g["Model-scoped kernel settings (ModelExecutionState)
RoPE, KV precision, shared layers, KV-Resident size"] g --> h["CPU expert pool
worker affinity installed"] h --> i["CUDA stream + kernel lease
providers pinned"] i --> j[".gexec resolution
never fails the load"] j --> k["Dense weights + output head"] k --> l["Expert tiers
embedded blob / pack / GGUF"] l --> m["Calibration + GPU expert cache"] m --> n["RAM-resident complement
zero-copy, pinned or NUMA-interleaved"] n --> o["Shared session state
KV staging, PLE, MTP, verifier, prefill"] o --> p["Tokenizer"] ``` Notes on the stages that are easy to get wrong: * **Ordering is a contract.** The pool installs worker affinity before any expert page is touched, so pages land on the intended NUMA node; the model-scoped kernel settings (`core::ModelExecutionState`, bound via `core::ScopedModelExecution`) are set before any weight is prepared, because the kernels read them while building quantized layouts and KV buffers; the kernel lease is taken before GEXEC resolution, so nothing can be unloaded underneath an artifact. Each `GuildModel` owns its own `ModelExecutionState` (shared with its `SessionState`) and its own `ExpertSource::layout()`, so multiple differently configured models can coexist in one process without overwriting each other's settings ([../quality/PHASE5.6_VALIDATION.md](../quality/PHASE5.6_VALIDATION.md)). * **Failure semantics.** A load failure returns `nullptr` with a message - it never throws to the caller, since the entry points are C ABI. An explicitly named `.gpack` must open; a `model.gpack` sidecar found next to a pack directory is a convenience and falls back to the shards. A `.gexec` can never fail a load: an unusable artifact is recorded as a fallback reason in the startup profile. * **Kernel selection.** Without GEXEC the default provider set is used. With GEXEC the artifact records which implementation won its measurement, and the runtime resolves that one - that is what makes an optimized run reproducible without re-tuning (see [GEXEC_CONTRACT.md](GEXEC_CONTRACT.md)). * **Two calibrations.** The first measures CPU/GPU/copy cost per layer and decides expert placement (or reuses the GEXEC heterogeneous plan if it was measured on this same fingerprint). The second runs after pinning and cache sizing, because the PCIe share has to be planned against the memory that actually exists. ## 2. Sessions `GuildModel::create_session()` returns a `GuildSession`: a handle, not a model copy. | Per session | Shared by every session | | --- | --- | | Drafting state (`SuffixDrafter`, `DraftPolicy`) | Weights, expert tiers, expert cache | | Cancellation flag | Device KV staging, PLE tables, verifier, prefill engine, tokenizer | | Its runner and kernel leases | The CUDA stream and the CPU expert pool | Two invariants hold for every entry point: * **Fail-closed readiness.** `ready` is cleared and re-checked when a generation starts; any failure after the first device work leaves it false, so later requests are refused instead of running on a half-valid model. * **Pinning.** The runner and kernel leases taken by the model and by each session keep the resolved providers loaded and their streams alive. Package disable or uninstall therefore fails, rather than forcing an unload under a running session ([PHASE2E_PACKAGE_LIFECYCLE.md](PHASE2E_PACKAGE_LIFECYCLE.md)). Generation is serialized by a model-wide lock: one process runs one generation at a time, and a session selects which state that generation uses. Solo `curl` scripts and the web app both see queueing, not parallelism. ## 3. One request ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant C as Client participant S as GuildSession participant V as Verifier participant M as MtpDrafter participant P as CPU expert pool participant G as GPU kernels C->>S: generate(request) S->>S: validate, take scopes, pin request thread S->>V: wait_commit / idle S->>S: session_zero (KV, PLE history) Note over S,G: prefill S->>G: batched prefill (or 1-token verifier passes) S->>M: prefill draft K/V loop until EOS, max_new_tokens, context limit or cancel S->>M: draft up to S-1 tokens S->>V: run(window of T tokens) V->>P: expert jobs for the window P->>G: GPU hit rows, CPU rows, peer rows V-->>S: outv (target tokens) S->>S: accept the longest prefix that matches the drafts S->>V: commit(accepted) S-->>C: stream accepted tokens end ``` * **Prefill** uses the batched engine (`BatchedPrefill`) when the architecture supports it and a sequential verifier loop otherwise. The prompt's *last* token is not consumed here: it becomes the first decode input, so the prompt's logits are produced by the decode path. * **A speculative window** is `T` tokens: the last accepted token plus up to `T-1` drafts proposed by the MTP drafter. `T` grows while the drafter's confidence stays above `spec_min_p`, and is 1 for the first window or when no drafter is configured. The verifier runs the window through the real model; a draft is accepted exactly when greedy decode would have produced it, and `commit(accepted)` keeps the accepted prefix and restores the session state (KV cells, PLE history, indexer state) for the rejected suffix. Declined drafts cost GPU work, never correctness. * **The expert pool** is where the model's cost lives: for each layer the pool thread decides which routed experts the primary GPU computes from its cache, which the peer GPU takes, and which the CPU computes from the pinned tier - all at once, so the two devices' work overlaps. * **Cancellation** is cooperative: `cancel()` sets a flag that the prefill and decode loops poll, and a disconnected streaming client stops the callback, which cancels the generation. ## 4. Why the hot path has no dispatch Resolution (runner, kernels, package binding, function pointers) all happens during load and session setup. The token and layer loops then execute pre-bound function pointers and launch captured CUDA graphs. This is not a style preference: at ~20-50 decode tokens per second on a mid-range GPU, a per-layer registry lookup or virtual call is measurable, and it is the reason the layering works through registries rather than base classes. ## See also * [README.md](README.md) - the component map and the artifact flow. * [MODULAR_RUNTIME.md](MODULAR_RUNTIME.md) - the three layers and the phase history. * [GEXEC_CONTRACT.md](GEXEC_CONTRACT.md) - what the artifact in stage 6 contains and when it is invalidated. * [GPACK_FORMAT.md](GPACK_FORMAT.md) - the container read in stage 2 and mapped in stage 7. * [../performance/PHASE4_PROFILING.md](../performance/PHASE4_PROFILING.md) - where the measured time in each stage goes.

# Modular Runtime Architecture

## Phase 3 extension infrastructure

[Runtime `.gkmodule` components](GKMODULE.md) reuse Phase 2E package, trust and
binding infrastructure. SDK 1.5 adds namespaced, versioned operations and a C
resolve/scratch/execute/release service. Runners can consume specialized operations
without adding model-specific operation enums to Core. Signed CPU and CUDA scan
modules exercise actual invocation, concurrent unload protection and graph/stream
lifetimes. Current RMD1 execution topology is unchanged; new complete model runners,
GPACK and GEXEC are described in [GPACK_FORMAT.md](GPACK_FORMAT.md) and
[GEXEC_CONTRACT.md](GEXEC_CONTRACT.md). Audio pipelines are later work.

## Phase 2 status

Independent native CPU experts, an SM 6.1 CUDA router, and a real Ornith model
description runner now build in separate repositories using standalone SDK 1.1.
They have passed combined real-model bitwise parity, including tested recurrent
state and host KV. Complete backend/architecture ownership transfer remains in
progress; see [EXTERNAL_BACKENDS.md](EXTERNAL_BACKENDS.md) for supported slices,
repository identities and remaining gates, and
[the measurements](../performance/EXTERNAL_KERNEL_PARITY.md) for the open
performance regression gate. The historical Phase 1 descriptions below must not
be read as proof of complete Phase 2 decoupling.

Guild separates inference execution into three strictly decoupled layers connected by a versioned C-compatible ABI (`include/guild/abi/kernel_abi.h`) and declarative `.gkernel` package manager (`include/guild/abi/gkernel_package.hpp`):

1. **Guild Core (`src/runtime/`, `src/memory/`, `src/plan/`, `src/spec/`, `src/server/`, `src/abi/`)**
   - GGUF/pack loading, memory hierarchy planning (VRAM, pinned host RAM, mmap/file expert tiers), KV/recurrent state lifecycle, speculative decoding orchestration (`SpeculativeController`, `SuffixDrafter`, `MtpDrafter`), tokenization, sampling, HTTP/OpenAI/Anthropic APIs, CLI, and `.gkernel` cryptographic package management (`GKernelPackageManager`).
    - Owns orchestration; the existing execution path still includes Qwen-shaped topology assumptions. Independent providers own the extracted arithmetic.

2. **Model Architecture Runners (`include/guild/model/runner.hpp`, `src/model/runner.cpp`)**
   - Define how a model family (`qwen4exp`, `qwen35moe`, or external ABI v1 runners) maps GGUF metadata and tensors into `ModelDescriptor`, validates architectural invariants (such as mandatory PLE tables or hybrid recurrent/full-attention intervals), declares required kernel operations (`required_ops`), and binds prefill/decode execution graphs.
   - Registered in `guild::model::ModelRunnerRegistry` (`runner.qwen4exp.v1`, `runner.qwen35moe.v1`, or external `.gkernel` runners).

3. **Hardware Kernels (`include/guild/kernels/registry.hpp`, `src/kernels/registry.cpp`, `src/core/`, `src/engine/`, `plugins/`)**
   - Architecture- and device-specific compute implementations for CPU (`AVX2`, `AVX-512F/BW/DQ/VL`, `AVX-512 VNNI`, `NEON`), NVIDIA CUDA (`SM 6.1` Pascal through `SM 9.0`), and AMD HIP (`gfx1100+`).
   - Registered in `guild::kernels::KernelRegistry` (both built-in and dynamically loaded `.gkernel` plugins) with explicit operation kinds (`guild_op_kind_t`), hardware/ISA/SM requirements, supported data types, batch ranges, scratch memory calculators, and numerical parity flags.

---

## Execution Lifecycle & Zero-Overhead Hot Path

The full sequence - startup stages, session creation, prefill, the decode and speculative window, and the
ownership rules - is in [EXECUTION_LIFECYCLE.md](EXECUTION_LIFECYCLE.md). The summary below is the modular-runtime
view of the same path.

To preserve single-token decode latency and batched prefill throughput, **neither virtual method dispatch nor hash-table/registry lookups occur inside layer or token loops**:

1. **Startup & Dynamic `.gkernel` Package Loading**
   - `KernelRegistry::instance()` registers built-in CPU (`builtin.guild-kernels-cpu`) and GPU (`builtin.guild-kernels-cuda` / `builtin.guild-kernels-amd`) kernel descriptors.
   - `ModelRunnerRegistry::instance()` registers `Qwen4ExpRunner` (`builtin.guild-kernels-qwen`) and `Qwen35MoERunner` (`builtin.guild-kernels-ornith`).
   - `GKernelPackageManager::instance().load_enabled_packages()` validates and dynamically loads (`dlopen` with `RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL`) all enabled `.gkernel` packages from `<GUILD_DATA_DIR>/kernels`, verifying Ed25519 signatures and per-artifact SHA-256 digests before executing `guild_plugin_entry_v1` via transactional registration.

2. **Model Load (`GuildModel::load`)**
   - Calls `GKernelPackageManager::instance().load_enabled_packages()` so any enabled external `.gkernel` runners and kernels are active.
   - Reads the GGUF header and resolves the architecture runner via `ModelRunnerRegistry::resolve_for_gguf()`.
   - Invokes `runner->validate_and_describe()` and `ModelRunnerRegistry::validate_runner_requirements()` to verify that every required operation has a hardware-compatible kernel on the host CPU/GPU.
   - Acquires per-package `SessionRunnerLease` and `SessionKernelLease` bound to the model's `cudaStream_t` (`main_stream`).

3. **Prefill & Verifier Binding (`BatchedPrefill::init` / `Verifier::init`)**
   - `BatchedPrefill::init()` calls `KernelRegistry::resolve_prefill_kernels()` **once**, resolving the highest-priority enabled kernel for each prefill operation (including any external `.gkernel` plugin providing `guild_prefill_kernel_ext_v1_t`, such as `ext.cuda.moe.router_topk_bf16`) into raw function pointers in `ResolvedPrefillKernels`, and attaches their `package_id`s to the model's `SessionKernelLease`.
   - `Verifier` captures pre-bound CUDA graphs for single-token and speculative verify windows.

4. **Token / Layer Inner Loops**
   - `BatchedPrefill::run()` invokes the pre-bound function pointers in `ResolvedPrefillKernels` and the pre-bound `ExpertPool::run_split_multi_native()` workers directly.
   - `Verifier::run()` launches captured CUDA graphs directly.

---

## Measured Phase 1 Performance Verification (`Ornith-1.5-35B-Q4_K_M`)

Measured on dual Intel Xeon Gold 6130 (32 physical cores / 64 threads, AVX-512F/BW/DQ/VL, no VNNI, 377 GiB DDR4 across 2 NUMA nodes) + NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070 (8 GiB VRAM, SM 6.1, CUDA 12.0, driver `580.178.04`), `Ornith-1.5-35B-Q4_K_M.gguf`, `context=32768`, `batch=256`, `generate=128`, 1 full-shaped warmup + 10 measured repetitions (`ornith_prefill_bench`):

| Prompt Tokens | Configuration | `9d77159` Baseline Prefill Median | Phase 1 Prefill Median (10 runs) | `9d77159` Baseline Decode Median | Phase 1 Decode Median (10 runs) |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `512` | Built-in (`gpu.moe.router_topk_native`) | `234.156 tok/s` | **`240.176 tok/s`** (`+2.57%`) | `42.977 tok/s` | **`43.427 tok/s`** (`+1.05%`) |
| `512` | External `.gkernel` (`ext.cuda.moe.router_topk_bf16`) | `234.156 tok/s` | **`240.089 tok/s`** (`+2.53%`) | `42.977 tok/s` | **`43.327 tok/s`** (`+0.81%`) |
| `2,048` | Built-in (`gpu.moe.router_topk_native`) | `220.620 tok/s` | **`231.634 tok/s`** (`+4.99%`) | `37.909 tok/s` | **`37.819 tok/s`** (`-0.24%`) |
| `4,096` | Built-in (`gpu.moe.router_topk_native`) | `209.275 tok/s` | **`216.998 tok/s`** (`+3.69%`) | `33.041 tok/s` | **`32.909 tok/s`** (`-0.40%`) |

Real-model end-to-end plugin verification (`ornith_gkernel_plugin_test`):
- `ext.guild-kernels-ornith-prefill@1.0.0` (`.gkernel` bundle signed with Ed25519) dynamically loaded via `GKernelPackageManager::install_package`.
- Verified `ext.cuda.moe.router_topk_bf16` bound in `BatchedPrefill` and executed 40 times per prompt across all 40 layers (`760` token-rows for a 20-token prompt).
- Full-vocabulary logits (`248,320` floats) and 8-token greedy continuation match the built-in kernel **bit-for-bit** (`std::memcmp == 0`).
- Active lease protection rejects `disable_package` / `remove_package` (`GUILD_STATUS_ERR_ACTIVE_SESSION_BUSY`) while bound, and cleanly falls back to `gpu.moe.router_topk_native` after lease release and `disable_package`.

---

## Roadmap: Phase 6 — Long-Context Decode Optimization (`8K–32K+`)

On 8 GiB VRAM cards (`GTX 1070`), Ornith-1.5-35B places its 10 full-attention layers' KV cache (`1,280 MiB` at 32K context in FP16) in pinned host RAM (`HostOnly` mode) and streams KV blocks over PCIe 3.0 x16 during decode (`42.98 tok/s` at 512 tokens -> `26.07 tok/s` at 8,192 tokens -> `18.05 tok/s` at 16,384 tokens). Phase 6 targets this long-context decode bottleneck via modular `.gkernel` and runtime enhancements:

1. **Multi-CTA Split-K FlashDecoding (`GUILD_OP_ATTN_DECODE`)**
   - Partition long sequence history (`N_kv >= 4096`) across multiple threadblocks per KV head (`split_k = 4..16`), computing partial online-softmax `(m_i, l_i, O_i)` tiles in parallel across all SMs and reducing across splits in a lightweight combine kernel.
2. **Asynchronous Double-Buffered Host-to-Device KV Tile Prefetching**
   - Overlap PCIe host-to-device KV tile transfers for full-attention layer `l_next` on a dedicated DMA stream while the GPU executes the 3 preceding Gated DeltaNet layers and CPU expert pool dispatch.
3. **Quantized Host KV Cache Streaming (`Q8_0` / `K8V4` for `Qwen35MoE`)**
   - Extend `GUILD_OP_KV_WRITE` and `GUILD_OP_ATTN_DECODE` in `Qwen35MoERunner` to support `Q8_0` and `K8V4` host-tier KV storage, cutting PCIe 3.0 KV read traffic by `2x–2.67x` at `8K–32K` context while preserving `512 MiB` VRAM safety reserve.

# Model Architecture Runners

## Phase 3 specialized operations

SDK 1.5 exposes `guild_operation_api_v1_t` through the optional `operations` tail
of the plugin host API. Runners can copy that table during init, resolve named
operation/version/capability requirements, and retain opaque bindings for their
execution resources. See [GKMODULE.md](GKMODULE.md) for tensor, scratch, device,
stream and unloading contracts. This service is available to `.gkernel` runners
and `.gkmodule` operation providers. It does not change the existing RMD1 model
description layout or claim support for arbitrary execution topologies.

SDK 1.1+ supplies the `RMD1` model-description extension in
`include/guild/abi/runner_abi.h`. The independent
[guild-runners-qwen](https://github.com/guild-inference/guild-runners-qwen)
repository (`v1.1.0`) owns the Qwen-family architecture runners (`qwen35moe`,
`qwen4exp`, `qwen2moe`, and `ornith`), using typed metadata/tensor callbacks,
copied C geometry values (`guild_runner_model_v1_t`), PLE metadata/tensor contract
validation, and vectorized `check_finite` instead of C++ runner subclasses inside
Core. When `GUILD_BUILTIN_QWEN_RUNNERS=ON` (default), `cmake/QwenRunnersBackend.cmake`
compiles `guild-runners-qwen` with `GUILD_BUNDLED_QWEN_RUNNERS=1` and registers
`runner.qwen4exp.v1` and `runner.qwen35moe.v1` through `AbiModelRunnerAdapter`.
When `GUILD_BUILTIN_QWEN_RUNNERS=OFF`, Core contains no built-in Qwen runners and
loads the signed `org.guild.runners.qwen` `.gkernel` package at runtime.
Ornith-1.5-35B passed bundled/external parity. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`UD-IQ4_XS`)
passed bundled-runner parity against the preserved engine; that test did not
establish external-only Qwen4Exp execution.

Headers & Implementation:
- [`include/guild/model/runner.hpp`](../../include/guild/model/runner.hpp)
- [`src/model/runner.cpp`](../../src/model/runner.cpp)
- [`include/guild/model/model_descriptor.hpp`](../../include/guild/model/model_descriptor.hpp)
- External Runner Plugin Example: [`plugins/runner_smoke_ext/runner_smoke_plugin.cpp`](../../plugins/runner_smoke_ext/runner_smoke_plugin.cpp)

Model Architecture Runners decouple model-family topology, GGUF metadata validation, and kernel requirements from Guild Core's memory management, scheduler, and server.

---

## 1. Built-In Runners

| Runner ID | Package ID | Architecture ID | Family | Key Architectural Features |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `runner.qwen4exp.v1` | `builtin.guild-kernels-qwen` | `qwen4exp` | `ModelFamily::Qwen4Exp` | 48 layers (36 Gated DeltaNet + 12 Quad-Sparse Attention, interval 4), 4-stream Hyper-Connections (`hc=4`), 512 routed experts (`top_k=10`) + 1 shared expert, mandatory Per-Layer Embeddings (`ple_compute`), Coupled-Draft MTP |
| `runner.qwen35moe.v1` | `builtin.guild-kernels-ornith` | `qwen35moe` | `ModelFamily::Qwen35MoE` | 40 layers (30 Gated DeltaNet + 10 Full GQA Attention, interval 4), single-stream residual (`hc=1`), 256 routed experts (`top_k=8`) + 1 shared expert, no PLE, native layer-wise batched prefill (`BatchedPrefill`) |

---

## 2. `IModelRunner` Interface & `AbiModelRunnerAdapter`

Every model runner implements `guild::model::IModelRunner` (either directly in C++ for built-in runners or via `AbiModelRunnerAdapter`, which wraps an external C ABI `guild_runner_desc_v1_t` registered from a `.gkernel` plugin):

- `runner_id()`: Stable versioned identifier (e.g., `"runner.qwen35moe.v1"`).
- `arch_id()`: Canonical architecture identifier (`"qwen4exp"`, `"qwen35moe"`, or custom architecture ID).
- `package_id()`: Owning `.gkernel` or built-in package identifier.
- `family()`: `ModelFamily` enum tag.
- `capabilities()`: Runner capability bitmask (`GUILD_RUNNER_CAP_*`).
- `matches_gguf(const GgufMetadata&)`: Inspects GGUF header keys (`general.architecture`, tensor names, layer counts) to determine if this runner supports the artifact.
- `validate_and_describe(const GgufModel&, ModelDescriptor&, std::string& err)`: Populates and validates `ModelDescriptor` from GGUF metadata and tensor headers.
- `configure_geometry(const ModelDescriptor&, core::ModelGeometry&, int64_t& top_k, std::string& err)`: Populates runtime geometry and enforces architectural invariants before device memory allocation.
- `required_operations(const ModelDescriptor&, const core::ModelGeometry&, const memory::ExecutionPlan&)`: Returns the list of `RunnerOpRequirement` entries (`op_name`, `category`, `backend`, `weight_dtype`, `activation_dtype`, `mandatory`) validated by `ModelRunnerRegistry::validate_runner_requirements()`.

---

## 3. Lifecycle & Per-Package Lease Safety

- `ModelRunnerRegistry::register_abi_runner(const guild_runner_desc_v1_t&, std::string& err)` validates `struct_size`, `abi_version` compatibility (`guild_abi_is_compatible`), and non-empty `runner_id`/`arch_id`, and deep-copies strings into `AbiModelRunnerAdapter`.
- When `GuildModel::load()` resolves a runner, it acquires a per-package `SessionRunnerLease(&ModelRunnerRegistry::instance(), runner->package_id())` and stores all resolved kernel `package_id`s in `RunnerExecutionPlan::resolved_package_ids` (held by `SessionKernelLease`).
- While any `GuildModel` or `GuildSession` holds a lease on a runner's `package_id`, `ModelRunnerRegistry::unregister_package()` and `GKernelPackageManager::disable_package()` / `remove_package()` refuse to unload the package with `GUILD_STATUS_ERR_ACTIVE_SESSION_BUSY`.

---

## 4. Building an External Runner `.gkernel` Plugin

See [`plugins/runner_smoke_ext/runner_smoke_plugin.cpp`](../../plugins/runner_smoke_ext/runner_smoke_plugin.cpp) for a complete external runner plugin compiled against `Guild::KernelSDK`:

1. Include `"guild/abi/kernel_abi.h"`.
2. Define a `guild_runner_desc_v1_t` with `struct_size = sizeof(guild_runner_desc_v1_t)`, `abi_version = GUILD_KERNEL_ABI_VERSION_V1`, `runner_id`, `arch_id`, `package_id`, and `probe_gguf` / `validate_model` / `build_execution_plan` callbacks.
3. Export `GUILD_PLUGIN_EXPORT guild_status_t guild_plugin_entry_v1(...)` and call `host_api->register_runner(host, &runner_desc, out_error)` inside the plugin's `init` callback.
4. Package with a `.gkmetadata` manifest declaring `"scope": "runner"` (or `"hybrid"`) and `"provided_runners": ["<runner_id>"]`, sign with `guild kernel sign`, and install with `guild kernel install`.

# Independent backends: verified migration slices

[Phase 3 runtime modules](GKMODULE.md) build with standalone SDK 1.5 and reuse
the same signing/loading system. The independent C99 scan example is in
`plugins/scan_module`; module and existing backend packages can coexist in one
store. The pinned CPU/CUDA/Qwen packages retain their current versions.

**Phase 2 is in progress.** These are functioning independent repositories and
packages, but complete CPU/CUDA/architecture decoupling is not finished.

Continuation: [CPU source ownership](CPU_BACKEND_OWNERSHIP.md) now uses pinned
independent sources for bundled builds and proves an external-only CPU arithmetic
configuration. The earlier preview scope and repository table below describe the
original migration slice, not the complete current CPU operation set.

[CUDA source ownership](CUDA_BACKEND_OWNERSHIP.md) now covers CDD1 dense,
CDA1 attention/recurrent and CDM1 MoE/device primitives in CUDA package 1.4.0,
using SDK 1.4.0. All three extracted groups passed external-only Ornith inference.
[Phase 2E package lifecycle](PHASE2E_PACKAGE_LIFECYCLE.md) and
[Phase 2E concurrency](PHASE2E_CONCURRENCY.md) establish reference-counted
provider bindings (`KernelBinding` and `std::shared_ptr<const IModelRunner>`),
cross-registry lifecycle transactions, durable `fsync` installation with
same-version immutability, and resource-aware KV staging. Current immutable
revisions are in `backends.lock.json`; the table below is the historical preview
snapshot.

| Repository | Original preview HEAD | Original verified scope |
|---|---|---|
| https://github.com/guild-inference/guild-kernels-cpu | `5c2a76f` | Native expert activation/hidden quantization, gate/up and down arithmetic; own pinned GGML build |
| https://github.com/guild-inference/guild-kernels-cuda | `aa1c565` | SM 6.1 BF16 router projection |
| https://github.com/guild-inference/guild-runners-qwen | `0ccff55` | Qwen-family model-description callbacks; real Ornith inference verified |

SDK/Core support starts at Guild `4b4ded0`. SDK package version is 1.1.0;
Kernel ABI remains v1.0.0. All three repositories have independent CMake projects,
tests, MIT attribution, manifest templates, signing instructions and CI build
workflows. Their build inputs are installed SDK files and declared dependencies.
They do not link private Core libraries or use its source headers.

Hosted CI passed independently for
[CPU](https://github.com/guild-inference/guild-kernels-cpu/actions/runs/38939706726),
[runner](https://github.com/guild-inference/guild-runners-qwen/actions/runs/38939705475),
and [CUDA compilation](https://github.com/guild-inference/guild-kernels-cuda/actions/runs/38939705014).
The actual CUDA execution test was local on the GTX 1070, not hosted CPU-only CI.

## Published preview artifacts

The [SDK 1.1 archive](https://github.com/guild-inference/Guild/releases/tag/kernel-sdk-v1.1.0-preview.1)
can be installed without building Core. Each external repository has an
`integration-v1.0.0-preview.1` prerelease with its signed integration-proof
packages and public verification receipt. CPU includes both 1.0.0 and 1.0.1.
These are explicitly test-signed previews, not production signing identities.
Full source SHAs, package/version names and bundle hashes are recorded in
`bench/results/external-kernels/package-verification.json`.

## Developer workflow

Install the SDK, then clone and build each repository separately using its README:

```sh
cmake -S sdk -B build-sdk -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/guild-sdk
cmake --install build-sdk
# In each external checkout:
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/guild-sdk
cmake --build build -j
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
cmake --install build --prefix "$PWD/build/package"
```

CUDA additionally needs its toolkit/compiler and `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=61`.
The CUDA manifest currently restricts support to SM 6.1; compiling another target
requires matching metadata and hardware validation. CPU has an AVX2/FMA/F16C
baseline and an explicit `GUILD_CPU_GGML_AVX512` variant. The measurements used the
AVX-512 variant on dual Xeon Gold 6130, with no VNNI requirement.

Use `guild kernel sign PACKAGE_DIR --key-id KEY --seed-file PRIVATE_FILE
--bundle OUTPUT.gkernel`, explicitly trust the corresponding public key, then
install with `guild kernel install`. Never distribute the seed. Default Core
trust no longer embeds the former published development key. Existing trust
stores must remove/revoke that development identity if they inherited it.
CI build artifacts are unsigned staging directories, not production releases;
signing is a separate explicit release step using the maintainer's private key.

Package identities:

- `org.guild.kernels.cpu@1.0.0` / `@1.0.1`, operation `external.cpu.native_expert.v1`.
- `org.guild.kernels.cuda@1.0.0`, operation `external.cuda.router.bf16.v1`.
- `org.guild.runners.qwen@1.0.0`, `runner.external.*.v1` providers.

`guild kernel active --json` shows provider IDs. The real-model test additionally
checks bound CPU/CUDA package IDs and DSO counters: installation alone is not
accepted as execution proof. Enabled package loading errors now fail model load
instead of being discarded in favor of built-in execution.

## Integration and independent updates

```sh
python3 tools/test_external_runner.py \
  --package /checkouts/guild-runners-qwen/build/package \
  --additional-package /checkouts/guild-kernels-cpu/build/package \
  --additional-package /checkouts/guild-kernels-cuda/build/package \
  --upgrade-package /checkouts/guild-kernels-cpu/build-upgrade/package \
  --artifact-output build-cuda12/external-dist
```

The driver creates a private temporary test key, explicitly trusts its public key,
signs and installs packages, and compares fresh-process inference against the
built-in reference. It then installs independently built CPU 1.0.1 and rolls back
to 1.0.0. The test checks descriptor version and actual callback execution at
each step and asserts that the Core executable's SHA-256 did not change. Test
bundles and their public verification identity can be retained with
`--artifact-output`; the private seed is deleted. These test identities are not
production release keys.

`GUILD_BUILTIN_QWEN_RUNNERS=OFF` removes built-in runner registration.
`GUILD_BUILTIN_NATIVE_CPU=OFF` replaces built-in native arithmetic with explicit
errors; a missing external native provider then fails model loading. Real Ornith
inference passed with both options off. Neither option disables the rest of Core's
CUDA backend or canonical planar Q2 implementation.

## Remaining requirements before Phase 2 completion

1. Finish the remaining legacy CUDA GEMM/MMQ and Qwen4Exp prefill extraction;
   extend external-only validation beyond the tested Ornith path.
2. Maintain the completed CPU source-ownership gates documented in
   `CPU_BACKEND_OWNERSHIP.md` while extending architecture coverage.
3. Move remaining Qwen topology/tensor-validation/state policy out of Core;
   validate Qwen4Exp/PLE/MTP with its actual model and the external runner.
4. Selection/lease and cross-registry transaction races, same-version
   immutability, durable `fsync` staging/registry commit, and 6-boundary fault
   injection + subprocess crash recovery are verified in
   [Phase 2E package lifecycle](PHASE2E_PACKAGE_LIFECYCLE.md),
   [Phase 2E concurrency](PHASE2E_CONCURRENCY.md), and
   [Phase 2E security and concurrency audit](../quality/PHASE2E_SECURITY_AND_CONCURRENCY_AUDIT.md).
5. Finish independent signed production release key provisioning outside CI.
6. Paired single-session and multi-session (`1, 2, 4, 8` sessions) performance
   evidence is recorded in
   [Phase 2E multi-session validation](../performance/PHASE2E_MULTI_SESSION_VALIDATION.md).

## Extension roadmap

- Phase 3: runtime `.gkmodule` components, namespaced capability negotiation,
  signed CPU/CUDA example operations and lifetime/dependency validation. See
  [the implementation contract](GKMODULE.md) and
  [validation record](../quality/PHASE3_MODULE_VALIDATION.md).
- Phase 4: GPACK artifact infrastructure (not implemented here).
- Phase 5: GEXEC generation and optimization (not implemented here).
- Later architecture work: complete runner-owned execution topology, specialized
  Qwen/GLM/Nemotron operations and Phase 7 Drama 3/audio integration. The Phase 3
  service is an operation foundation, not a complete implementation of these models.

# GPACK v1 Model Packaging Format (`GPCK` / `GPKE`)

GPACK (`.gpack`) is Guild's portable, versioned, hardware-independent model container format introduced in Phase 4. It consolidates multi-shard GGUF or safetensors models, pre-parsed binary tensor and dense/expert layout indices, precomputed `GBT1` binary tokenizer assets, and optional auxiliary components (PLE n-gram tables and MTP speculative draft layers) into a single page-aligned, `mmap`-ready artifact.

GPACK is **strictly hardware-independent**: it never embeds machine-specific CUDA SM architectures, host NUMA node bindings, or autotuned kernel winners. Hardware-specific artifacts belong exclusively to the disposable GEXEC (`GEXC`) cache layer (`docs/architecture/GEXEC_CONTRACT.md`).

---

## 1. Binary Container Layout

All integers in GPACK v1 are little-endian. All data payload sections are aligned to `4096` bytes (OS page and `O_DIRECT` sector alignment) or `64` bytes (CPU cacheline and AVX-512 alignment).

```text
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+ 0x0000
| GPackHeaderV1 (64 bytes, magic = "GPCK" / 0x4B435047)                 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+ 0x0040 (aligned)
| Section 0: MetadataKvBin       (64B aligned, binary key-value table)  |
| Section 1: TensorIndexBin      (64B aligned, sorted tensor directory) |
| Section 2: DenseIndexBin       (64B aligned, pre-parsed dense rows)   |
| Section 3: DensePackBlob       (4096B aligned, packed dense weights)  |
| Section 4: NativeDenseIndexBin (64B aligned, single-arena MMVQ index) |
| Section 5: NativeDenseBlob     (4096B aligned, contiguous MMVQ arena) |
| Section 6: EmbedBlob           (4096B aligned, token_embd.weight)     |
| Section 7: HeadBlob            (4096B aligned, output.weight)         |
| Section 8: PleBlob             (4096B aligned, optional PLE table)    |
| Section 9: ExpertLayoutBin     (64B aligned, per-layer expert table)  |
| Section 10: ExpertBlobs        (4096B aligned, optional [l][e] blobs) |
| Section 11: TokenizerBin       (64B aligned, GBT1 binary tokenizer)   |
| Section 12: TokenizerAssets    (64B aligned, raw tokenizer files)     |
| Section 13: MtpBlob            (4096B aligned, optional MTP draft)    |
| Section 14: ManifestJson       (64B aligned, guild.gpack.v1 JSON)     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+ section_table_offset (64B aligned)
| GPackSectionEntryV1[section_count] (96 bytes per entry, with SHA-256) |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+ footer_offset (64B aligned)
| GPackFooterV1 (64 bytes, magic = "GPKE" / 0x454B5047)                 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+ EOF
```

### Header (`GPackHeaderV1`, 64 bytes)
- `magic`: `0x4B435047` (`"GPCK"`)
- `format_version`: `1` (`uint16_t`)
- `min_reader_version`: `1` (`uint16_t`) — readers with `kGPackVersionV1 < min_reader_version` fail closed with a clear version error.
- `flags`: Bitmask of `GPackFlags`:
  - `GUILD_GPACK_FLAG_LITTLE_ENDIAN` (`1 << 0`)
  - `GUILD_GPACK_FLAG_HAS_DENSE_PACK` (`1 << 1`)
  - `GUILD_GPACK_FLAG_HAS_NATIVE_DENSE` (`1 << 2`)
  - `GUILD_GPACK_FLAG_HAS_EXPERT_BLOBS` (`1 << 3`)
  - `GUILD_GPACK_FLAG_HAS_TOKENIZER_BIN` (`1 << 4`)
  - `GUILD_GPACK_FLAG_HAS_MTP` (`1 << 5`)
  - `GUILD_GPACK_FLAG_HAS_PLE` (`1 << 6`)
  - `GUILD_GPACK_FLAG_EXTERNAL_EXPERTS` (`1 << 7`)
- `section_count`: Number of `GPackSectionEntryV1` records in the section directory.
- `section_table_offset`: Byte offset of the section directory.
- `manifest_offset`, `manifest_size`: Byte offset and length of the canonical `ManifestJson` section.
- `total_file_size`: Exact expected file size in bytes (detects file truncation or trailing garbage immediately upon open).

### Section Directory Entry (`GPackSectionEntryV1`, 96 bytes)
- `kind`: `GPackSectionKind` (`uint32_t`)
- `flags`: Reserved section flags (`uint32_t`)
- `offset`: Byte offset from start of file (`uint64_t`, must be a multiple of `alignment`)
- `size`: Section payload size in bytes (`uint64_t`)
- `alignment`: Required byte alignment (`64` or `4096`)
- `item_count`: Number of logical items in the section (`uint64_t`)
- `sha256[32]`: Full SHA-256 digest of the section payload bytes
- `name[24]`: Null-terminated ASCII section identifier

### Footer (`GPackFooterV1`, 64 bytes)
- `manifest_offset`, `section_table_offset`, `total_payload_bytes`
- `manifest_sha256[32]`: SHA-256 digest of the `ManifestJson` section (which itself embeds the SHA-256 digests of every other section, forming a two-level Merkle tree over the entire file).
- `footer_magic`: `0x454B5047` (`"GPKE"`)

---

## 2. Precomputed Portable Sections

### 2.1 `DenseIndexBin` & `DensePackBlob`
Replaces text parsing of `index.txt` (3 separate `sscanf` passes during GGUF+pack load) with a binary table of `GPackDenseRowV1` records containing precomputed `skip_in_native` flags and both uncompacted (`dense_pool_bytes`) and compacted (`dense_compacted_pool_bytes`) VRAM arena sizes. `WeightTable::load_gpack` copies or expands BF16/F16->F32 weights directly from the `mmap`'d `DensePackBlob` into VRAM without opening external files.

### 2.2 `NativeDenseIndexBin` & `NativeDenseBlob`
Replaces 262–305 individual `cudaMalloc` and `cudaMemcpy` calls in `NativeDense::load` with a pre-laid-out 256-byte-aligned contiguous weight arena (`native_dense_arena_bytes`). At model load time, `NativeDense::load_gpack` allocates **one** device arena via `cudaMalloc` and uploads all native MMVQ weights in **one** `cudaMemcpyAsync` transfer.

### 2.3 `EmbedBlob`, `HeadBlob`, and `PleBlob`
Each section begins with a 64-byte `GPackSingleTensorHeaderV1` (`ggml_type`, `ne0`, `ne1`, `byte_size`, `data_offset = 64`), followed immediately by the tensor payload aligned within the 4096-byte section.
- `NativeEmbed::load_gpack` and `NativeHead::load_gpack` bind directly to the `mmap`'d pointers without re-opening GGUF shards.
- `PleTable::open_raw` binds the PLE n-gram table at its exact file offset inside the `.gpack` container, supporting both `PleIo::Direct` (4 KiB page-aligned unbuffered SSD reads + set-associative row cache) and `PleIo::Mmap`.

### 2.4 `ExpertLayoutBin` & `ExpertBlobs` (Embedded vs. External Modes)
GPACK supports two routed-expert storage modes:
1. **Embedded Experts (default)**: All routed experts across all layers (`n_layers * n_expert`) are concatenated in canonical `[gate_slice | up_slice | down_slice]` order into the 4096-byte-aligned `ExpertBlobs` section.
   - Enables true single-file portability.
   - Supports both NUMA-interleaved RAM resident caching (`FileExpertSource::open_gpack`) and zero-copy direct `mmap` execution (`GUILD_EXPERT_MMAP=1`).
2. **External Experts (`--external-experts`)**: `ExpertLayoutBin` records the pre-validated per-layer byte offsets and shard filenames in the source GGUF shards alongside the `.gpack` file, omitting `ExpertBlobs`.
   - Builds in ~12 seconds for Ornith-1.5-35B (1.54 GiB `.gpack` instead of 19.71 GiB) without duplicating 18–55 GiB of expert weights on disk.

### 2.5 `TokenizerBin` (`GBT1`) & `TokenizerAssets`
The `TokenizerBin` section stores the precomputed `GBT1` binary tokenizer (`magic = 0x31544247`):
- Header (`GbtHeaderV1`): `vocab_size`, `n_merges`, `eos_token_id`, `flags`, `vocab_blob_bytes`, `chat_template_bytes`.
- Contiguous `uint32_t offsets[vocab_size + 1]` and `uint8_t token_types[vocab_size]`.
- Contiguous UTF-8 vocabulary string blob (`vocab_blob_bytes`).
- Pre-resolved integer BPE merge triples `int32_t triples[n_merges][3]` (`left_token_id`, `right_token_id`, `merged_token_id`) ordered by merge rank `0 .. n_merges - 1`.
- Raw Jinja chat template string (`chat_template_bytes`).

Loading `GBT1` avoids parsing 11 MiB of `vocab.json`, `merges.txt`, and `token_type.json`, reducing 248,320-token vocabulary initialization from `355 ms` to `69 ms` (**5.1x faster**) while producing 100% identical token IDs.

---

## 3. Atomic Conversion, Verification, and GGUF Fallback

- **Crash-Safe Atomic Conversion**: `GPackBuilder::build` writes to `<output_path>.tmp.<pid>`, flushes and `fsync`s the file descriptor, verifies the written container headers and footer before closing, and atomically renames it to `<output_path>`. Any conversion failure unlinks the temporary file so a partial `.gpack` never exists at the destination path.
- **Two-Tier Integrity Verification**:
  - *Quick open* (`verify_all_hashes = false`, used at normal startup): Validates header/footer magics, format version, `min_reader_version`, exact `total_file_size`, section bounds/alignments, and the `ManifestJson` SHA-256 (~1–2 ms).
  - *Full verification* (`verify_all_hashes = true` or `guild verify <file.gpack>`): Streams every section payload through SHA-256 and checks every `GPackSectionEntryV1::sha256` digest.
- **Automatic GGUF Fallback**: In `GuildModel::load`, if `paths.gpack_path` is unreadable or fails validation **and** `paths.primary_model_path` (GGUF) is present, Guild logs a warning and falls back cleanly to the GGUF + pack loader. If no fallback GGUF is configured, `GuildModel::load` fails closed with the exact validation error.

---

## 4. CLI Usage

```bash
# Convert a single or multi-shard GGUF (+ pack directory) to a self-contained .gpack:
guild convert /path/to/Ornith-1.5-35B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --pack-dir /path/to/packs/ornith-1.5-35b \
  --name ornith-1.5-35b \
  -o /path/to/ornith-1.5-35b.gpack --json
```

# GEXEC v1 Hardware-Specialized Execution Contract (`GEXC`) GPACK (`.gpack`) is the portable model artifact. GEXEC (`.gexec`, magic `GEXC`) is a disposable, hardware- and runtime-bound execution cache. Phase 5 adds a binary container, an offline optimizer, CPU expert providers, and runtime loading to the Phase 4 contract. Header: [`include/guild/gexec/gexec_contract.hpp`](../../include/guild/gexec/gexec_contract.hpp) Implementation: [`src/gexec/gexec_contract.cpp`](../../src/gexec/gexec_contract.cpp) Test Suite: [`tests/core/gexec_contract_test.cpp`](../../tests/core/gexec_contract_test.cpp) Optimizer: [`src/gexec/gexec_optimizer.cpp`](../../src/gexec/gexec_optimizer.cpp) Lifecycle and kernel tests: [`tests/core/gexec_optimizer_test.cpp`](../../tests/core/gexec_optimizer_test.cpp) --- ## 1. Separation of Concerns: GPACK vs. GEXEC | Concern | GPACK (`.gpack` — Portable) | GEXEC (`.gexec` — Machine-Bound Cache) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Lifespan** | Immutable source-of-truth model container; distributable across machines | Disposable local optimization artifact; rebuilt automatically when invalidated | | **Weights** | Canonical GGML/Guild quantization blocks (`[gate \| up \| down]` per expert) | Hardware-specific repacked layouts (e.g. interleaved `[gate_row_i \| up_row_i]`, SIMD tile transposes) | | **Kernels** | Declares required abstract operations (`guild_op_kind_t`) and capability flags | Locks autotuned `impl_id` / `package_id` winners per `(op, phase, dtype, M, N, K)` | | **Memory & NUMA** | Agnostic to host RAM size, NUMA sockets, or VRAM capacity | Stores calibrated CPU/GPU/PCIe latencies, NUMA interleave/THP policy, and VRAM expert slot assignments | | **Compiled Graphs** | None | Stores CUDA/HIP runtime/driver/SM-keyed graph and kernel compilation cache keys | --- ## 2. Hardware Fingerprint & Cache Identity (`GExecArtifactIdentity`) Every GEXEC artifact is bound to a `GExecArtifactIdentity` whose deterministic SHA-256 cache key (`compute_cache_key()`) incorporates: 1. **`format_version`**: `kGExecVersionV1` (`1`) 2. **`gpack_manifest_sha256`**: 64-hex SHA-256 digest of the source `.gpack` manifest (which covers all section SHA-256 digests). 3. **`core_abi_version` & `module_abi_version`**: Kernel ABI (`GUILD_KERNEL_ABI_VERSION_V1`) and Module ABI (`GUILD_MODULE_ABI_VERSION_V1`). 4. **`runner_id` & `runner_version`**: Resolved `RMD1` model runner identity (e.g. `guild.runner.qwen3_5_moe.v1`). 5. **`bound_packages`**: Canonical sorted list of `(package_id, version, payload_sha256)` for all loaded `.gkernel` and `.gkmodule` packages. 6. **`GExecHardwareFingerprint`**: - Host CPU architecture (`x86_64`, `aarch64`), ISA feature flags (`AVX2`, `FMA`, `F16C`, `AVX512F`, `AVX512BW`, `AVX512VL`, `AVX512VNNI`), L1d/L2/L3 cache sizes, physical core count, and NUMA node count. - GPU device name, compute capability (`gpu_cc_major`, `gpu_cc_minor`), SM count, total VRAM bytes, L2 cache bytes, memory bus width, and CUDA driver/runtime versions. 7. **Execution Plan Parameters**: `kv_format`, `kv_mode`, `max_context`, `prefill_batch`, and `mtp_spec_tokens`. --- ## 3. Deterministic Invalidation Rules & Fallback Behavior `GExecArtifactIdentity::validate(cached, current, out_reason)` checks compatibility (`GExecInvalidationReason`); the container reader also checks payload integrity: 1. `MagicOrVersionMismatch`: `cached.format_version != current.format_version` 2. `GPackIdentityMismatch`: `cached.gpack_manifest_sha256 != current.gpack_manifest_sha256` 3. `CoreAbiMismatch`: `cached.core_abi_version != current.core_abi_version || cached.module_abi_version != current.module_abi_version` 4. `RunnerIdentityMismatch`: `cached.runner_id != current.runner_id || cached.runner_version != current.runner_version` 5. `ModuleOrKernelDigestMismatch`: Any bound `.gkernel` or `.gkmodule` package ID, version, or payload SHA-256 differs. 6. `CpuIsaMismatch`: Host CPU architecture or required SIMD ISA bitmask differs. 7. `NumaTopologyMismatch`: Number of allowed NUMA nodes differs. 8. `GpuArchitectureMismatch`: GPU device count, compute capability (`SM major.minor`), SM count, or GPU name differs. 9. `CudaRuntimeOrDriverMismatch`: CUDA runtime version differs or driver version was downgraded. 10. `ExecutionPlanMismatch`: `kv_format`, `kv_mode`, `max_context`, `prefill_batch`, or `mtp_spec_tokens` differs. 11. `CorruptedDigest`: Header, section table, or payload SHA-256 verification fails on load. **Fallback Rule**: An invalid, missing, or corrupt GEXEC cache **never** aborts model loading. Guild logs the exact `GExecInvalidationReason` and falls back to portable GPACK (or GGUF) execution and runtime operation negotiation. --- ## 4. Phase 5 Preparation Interfaces Implemented in Phase 4 ### 4.1 Offline Expert Gate/Up Row Interleaving (`GExecExpertPackMode::GateUpRowInterleaved`) In canonical GGUF/GPACK expert blobs, an expert's weights are stored as `[gate_rows (n_ff * gate_row_bytes) | up_rows (n_ff * up_row_bytes) | down_rows]`. During CPU expert evaluation, each worker thread computes `gate[row]` and `up[row]` simultaneously for the same quantized input activation `q8`, requiring two separate memory streams separated by `n_ff * gate_row_bytes` (~400–800 KiB). - `pack_expert_gate_up_interleaved(src_blob, dst_blob, n_ff, gate_row_bytes, up_row_bytes, down_bytes)` interleaves row `i` of `gate` immediately adjacent to row `i` of `up` (`[gate_row_0 | up_row_0 | gate_row_1 | up_row_1 | ... | down_rows]`), halving CPU prefetcher stream pressure while keeping `down_rows` contiguous. - `unpack_expert_gate_up_interleaved(...)` restores the exact canonical layout (verified bit-for-bit in `gexec_contract_test`: `128 us` per 1.2 MiB expert blob). ### 4.2 Operation-Registry Autotune Lock Table (`GExecAutotuneTable`) - `autotune_operation(op_kind, operation_name, phase, backend, quant_type, m, n, k, required_caps)` queries `OperationRegistry::instance()` (Phase 3) for all registered kernel candidates matching the operation and hardware capabilities, records the selected `impl_id`, `package_id`, and `fallback_impl_id`, and serializes the table with a tamper-evident `payload_sha256` digest. ### 4.3 NUMA / THP & Heterogeneous Placement Plan (`GExecHeterogeneousPlan`) - Captures the calibrated CPU/GPU/PCIe expert latencies (`calibrated_cpu_ms`, `calibrated_gpu_ms`, `calibrated_copy_ms`), per-layer GPU eligibility (`gpu_layers`), PCIe offload numerators (`pcie_numerators`), VRAM expert cache slot count (`expert_cache_slots`), NUMA policy (`interleave` vs. `process`), and 2 MiB transparent hugepage (`use_thp_hugepages`) selection with SHA-256 integrity verification. ### 4.4 Compilation Cache Key (`GExecCompilationKey`) - Produces a deterministic 64-hex SHA-256 key over `(cuda_runtime_version, cuda_driver_version, gpu_cc_major, gpu_cc_minor, kernel_package_sha256, compile_flags, graph_topology_signature)` for Phase 5 offline/persistent CUDA graph and kernel binary caching. ## 5. Binary container and installation The little-endian v1 file has a 64-byte header followed by 64-byte section entries. The header contains the total length and SHA-256 of the header fields and section table. Each entry records kind, flags, alignment, offset, length and SHA-256. Metadata sections are JSON, aligned to 64 bytes. `PackedExpertsBlob` is optional and aligned to at least 4096 bytes. The reader checks bounds, overlap, alignment, duplicate section kinds, metadata identities and embedded expert lengths. Sections: `IdentityAndManifest`, `AutotuneTable`, `HeterogeneousPlan`, `WorkspaceRecipe`, `CompilationProvenance`, `ExpertPackMeta`, `PackedExpertsBlob`, and `DiagnosticLog`. The JSON description is in [`schemas/gexec.v1.schema.json`](../../schemas/gexec.v1.schema.json). Writers hold `.lock`, write a same-directory temporary file, flush it, and atomically replace the destination. Existing readers keep their mapped snapshot. Lock files remain in place to avoid locking different inodes under the same pathname. Cache cleanup takes the same writer lock. Built-in provider identities include a configure-time SHA-256 of runtime, kernel and runner source bytes plus compiler options. Installed packages use their package payload digests. Changing a built-in implementation therefore invalidates its artifacts even in an uncommitted development build. ## 6. Optimizing and using a model ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph produce["Produce (offline, once per host)"] opt["guild optimize model.gpack --mode auto"] meas["Measure: heterogeneous plan,
autotune table, packed experts,
workspace recipe, provenance"] art["Write model.gexec
lock, temp file, atomic rename"] opt --> meas --> art end subgraph use["Use (every load)"] src["Source: --gexec, GUILD_GEXEC_PATH,
keyed cache, sibling .gexec"] id{"identity matches
this container, ABI and host?"} frozen["Frozen kernel selection,
packed expert layout"] fallback["GPACK layout,
reason in the startup profile"] src --> id id -- yes --> frozen id -- no --> fallback end subgraph maintain["Maintain"] regen["--section autotune|plan|workspace|provenance
regenerates one section"] clean["guild cache-clean
takes the writer lock"] disable["GUILD_DISABLE_GEXEC=1
or a changed model/ABI/host"] end art -.-> src art -.-> regen clean -.-> art disable -.-> fallback ``` ```sh guild optimize model.gpack --mode auto --context 2048 --prefill-batch 64 -o model.gexec guild inspect model.gexec --json guild verify model.gexec --gpack model.gpack --json guild run model.gpack --gexec model.gexec guild cache-clean --dir .gexec_cache --model model.gpack ``` The context, KV configuration, prefill batch and speculative-token count must match the runtime plan. `--spec` sets the speculative-token count. `--gexec` is also accepted by `serve`; runtime loading otherwise checks the keyed cache, `GUILD_GEXEC_PATH`, and a sibling `.gexec`. `GUILD_DISABLE_GEXEC=1` disables it. An incompatible or incomplete artifact falls back to GPACK with a reason in the startup profile. Modes control sampling: `skip` performs no optimization; `quick` uses two warmups and five timed samples; `auto` uses three and nine; `exhaustive` uses six and nineteen. Each candidate must support the host and pass bitwise gate/up, quantization and down-projection checks on real model weights for every distinct expert format. Single-expert timings, weighted by each format's layer count, rank the valid candidates. A counterbalanced multi-worker pool and combine trial then tests every valid candidate against the portable baseline at the model's decode token-group size and checks bitwise parity before selecting the winner. The portable provider remains the fallback. Pool timings are recorded separately from full-model throughput. Four providers implement fused or row-interleaved execution with AVX2 or AVX-512. They have lower registry priority than the ordinary CPU provider; the artifact freezes the chosen ID and version. The interleaved layout is consumed directly by the CPU kernels and by the native MMQ prefill path. The fused expert pool publishes quantized gate/up results with release/acquire synchronization before scheduling down-projection slices. GPU decode cache and PCIe-offload paths currently require portable expert layout. An interleaved artifact falls back when those paths are requested. Zero-copy GPACK mmap likewise needs a portable layout, unless the artifact contains its own packed expert blob. ## 7. Budgets, resume and regeneration `--max-time` limits seconds; `--max-memory` and `--max-disk` limit bytes. `--embed-experts` streams packed weights into the artifact using an expert-sized working set. Without it, the runtime interleaves during its ordinary expert load. The portable GPACK is never rewritten. Each completed pass checkpoints to `.progress.json`. The checkpoint has an identity and digest; stale or corrupt checkpoints are ignored. Budget exhaustion may install a partial artifact for inspection and resume. Partial artifacts are not activated for inference. `--no-resume` restarts optimization. `guild optimize model.gpack -o model.gexec --section workspace` regenerates one section. Supported names are `autotune`, `plan`, `workspace`, and `provenance`. Retuning that changes an embedded layout requires a complete rebuild. Selective regeneration streams the existing expert section and keeps unrelated section digests intact. The current workspace recipe records dense arena sizes. GPU/PCIe calibration and graph capture still run through the runtime when the artifact has no measured calibration or captured graph. The optimizer does not label CPU pool timings as end-to-end decode savings or invent a break-even token count. ## 8. Measured results Measured on a dual-socket Intel Xeon Gold 6130 (32 physical cores, 64 threads, 2 NUMA nodes) with an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070 (8 GiB GDDR5, SM 6.1) and NVMe SSD (`/mnt/models-ssd`), using counterbalanced A/B/B/A runs of `ornith_prefill_bench` (`--runs 2`, steady-state run 2 reported per trial): - **Ornith-1.5-35B** (`ornith-1.5-35b-ext.gpack`, 40 layers, 256 experts/layer, 8 active, 512 prompt tokens, 128 generated tokens, `--batch 512`, `--spec 0`): `guild optimize --mode auto` took `272.3 ms` (`19,832 B` artifact) and selected `cpu.expert_pool.gexec_fused_avx512`. - Load time: `6,232.3 ms` portable vs. `6,190.5 ms` GEXEC. - Prefill: `2,248.5 ms` (`227.3 tok/s`) portable vs. `2,230.5 ms` (`229.1 tok/s`) GEXEC. - Decode (128 tokens): `2,736.6 ms` (`46.77 tok/s`) portable vs. `2,568.4 ms` (`49.84 tok/s`, `+6.56%`) GEXEC. - CPU expert pool + combine per 128 decode tokens: `decode_cpu_pool_ms` dropped from `1,023.5 ms` to `850.0 ms` (`-17.0%`), `decode_cpu_quant_ms` from `69.4 ms` to `6.2 ms`, and `decode_cpu_validation_ms` from `55.7 ms` to `3.7 ms`. - Memory: `2.41 GiB` VRAM on both; `21.6 GiB` vs. `21.7 GiB` peak host RSS. - Output parity: identical token IDs across all four runs. - Break-even: `1.314 ms/token` saved in decode pays back the `272.3 ms` optimization pass after `208` generated tokens. - **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next** (`qwen3.8-flash-next-ext.gpack`, 48 layers, 512 experts/layer, 10 active, 512 prompt tokens, 64 generated tokens, `--batch 512`, `--spec 1`): `guild optimize --mode auto` took `604.4 ms` (`23,684 B` artifact) and selected `cpu.expert_pool.gexec_fused_avx512`. - Load time: `9,481.7 ms` portable vs. `9,428.4 ms` GEXEC. - Prefill: `5,364.5 ms` (`95.26 tok/s`) portable vs. `5,357.2 ms` (`95.39 tok/s`) GEXEC. - Decode (64 tokens, 38 MTP windows): `2,906.7 ms` (`22.02 tok/s`) portable vs. `2,825.0 ms` (`22.66 tok/s`, `+2.90%`) GEXEC. - CPU expert pool + combine per 64 decode tokens: `decode_cpu_pool_ms` dropped from `1,258.9 ms` to `1,175.0 ms` (`-6.7%`), `decode_cpu_down_ms` from `355.5 ms` to `264.4 ms` (`-25.6%`), `decode_cpu_quant_ms` from `21.4 ms` to `1.4 ms`, and `decode_cpu_validation_ms` from `56.0 ms` to `5.5 ms`. - Memory: `7.14 GiB` VRAM on both; `64.7 GiB` vs. `65.3 GiB` peak host RSS. - Output parity: identical token IDs across all four runs. - Break-even: `1.276 ms/token` saved in decode pays back the `604.4 ms` optimization pass after `474` generated tokens.

# Guild Kernel ABI v1 and standalone SDK 1.5

SDK 1.5 adds the optional [Phase 3 operation service](GKMODULE.md), declared in
`include/guild/abi/module_abi.h`. Kernel/runner descriptors retain their v1 layout;
the host callback table has an optional, size-checked tail pointer. Namespaced
GOP1 operations use the existing registry and reference-counted bindings.

Normative headers:

- `include/guild/abi/kernel_abi.h`: frozen Kernel ABI v1 descriptors and registration.
- `include/guild/abi/runner_abi.h`: optional `RMD1` model-description extension.
- `include/guild/abi/cpu_expert_abi.h`: optional `CPE1` native expert arithmetic.
- `include/guild/abi/cpu_backend_abi.h`: extended CPU backend callbacks.
- `include/guild/abi/cuda_dense_abi.h`, `cuda_attn_abi.h`, `cuda_moe_abi.h`:
  optional `CDD1`, `CDA1`, `CDM1` CUDA execution groups.

The standalone SDK builds without a compiler, GPU toolkit, GGML or Core runtime:

```sh
cmake -S sdk -B build-sdk -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/guild-sdk
cmake --install build-sdk
cpack --config build-sdk/CPackConfig.cmake -B build-sdk
```

External projects using all current contracts use `find_package(GuildKernelSDK 1.4 REQUIRED CONFIG)` and
`guild_configure_gkernel_plugin(target)`. The installed files contain only public
C headers, the manifest schema and CMake configuration. `CUDA_RUNTIME_LIBRARY
Shared` keeps plugins on the shared CUDA runtime. The helper itself does not
prove unloading safety; Core must still retain the package and finish stream work.

## Versioning and compatibility

`GUILD_KERNEL_ABI_MAKE_VERSION(major, minor, patch)` packs 8/12/12 bits:
major at bits 24–31, minor at 12–23, patch at 0–11. ABI v1.0.0 is `0x01000000`.
The `GUILD_MAKE_ABI_VERSION` and `GUILD_ABI_VERSION_*` aliases use the same format.
SDK version 1.4 does **not** change the layout or numeric ABI version of existing
v1 descriptors. New functionality uses size/tag/version-checked extension payloads.

Plugins export `guild_plugin_entry_v1` (`GUILD_PLUGIN_ENTRY_SYMBOL_V1`) with the
`guild_plugin_entry_fn` signature and `guild_plugin_descriptor_v1_t` result.
No STL objects, private C++ classes or exceptions cross the public boundary.
Plugins must handle their own initialization failures and return a status.

## Status values (matching kernel_abi.h)

| Code | Value |
|---|---:|
| OK | 0 |
| INVALID_ARGUMENT | -1 |
| ABI_MISMATCH | -2 |
| UNSUPPORTED_HARDWARE | -3 |
| CAPABILITY_MISMATCH | -4 |
| MISSING_RUNNER | -5 |
| MISSING_KERNEL | -6 |
| DUPLICATE_REGISTRATION | -7 |
| DEPENDENCY_MISSING | -8 |
| INVALID_TENSOR | -9 |
| BUFFER_LIFETIME | -10 |
| OUT_OF_MEMORY | -11 |
| EXECUTION_FAILED | -12 |
| NONFINITE_OUTPUT | -13 |
| SECURITY_VIOLATION | -14 |
| ACTIVE_SESSION_BUSY | -15 |
| INTERNAL | -99 |

Names except `OK` have the `GUILD_STATUS_ERR_` prefix; `OK` is `GUILD_STATUS_OK`.
`guild_error_info_t` carries a fixed message buffer and optional component name.

## Extension contracts

### Legacy prefill

The old seven-pointer `direct_fn_table` is frozen. It is a legacy C++ contract,
including `RopeScaling&`, and must not be used as the public interface of a new
standalone backend. The public `guild_prefill_kernel_ext_v1_t` has a 12-byte
`guild_prefill_ext_header_t` (`struct_size`, `tag`, `version`) followed by `gdn_ab`
and `router_projection` function pointers. Its tag is `0x50464b45` (`PFKE`) and
version is 1. It is not a `guild_ext_header_t` linked list.

### Model description (`RMD1`)

A runner descriptor attaches `guild_runner_model_ext_v1_t` through `next_ext`.
Core copies the extension before plugin init's stack storage can disappear.
It provides recognition, model description, numerical validation and selection
priority. Distinct runner IDs may cover the same architecture at different
priorities; enabled higher-priority providers are considered first.

`guild_model_reader_v1_t` exposes read-only numeric/string metadata and tensor
shape callbacks. Core retains all GGUF files and payloads. Description values
are copied into `guild_runner_model_v1_t`, including model dimensions, recurrent
geometry, periodic full-attention interval, MoE parameters, RoPE, PLE requirements,
prefill strategy and canonical tensor roles. No registry lookup occurs per token.

The current execution contract is limited to canonical tensor names and periodic
hybrid topology. Unsupported mappings are rejected explicitly. This extension
does not yet move every layer equation, tensor validation rule or state policy
out of Core. See `EXTERNAL_BACKENDS.md` for the remaining extraction gates.

### Native CPU experts (`CPE1`)

`guild_cpu_expert_ext_v1_t` attaches to `GUILD_OP_BATCHED_EXPERT_EXEC`. It has
size/tag/version fields and four synchronous callbacks: activation quantization,
hidden quantization, gate/up rows and down rows. `guild_cpu_expert_format_v1_t`
contains fixed-width scalar format values and byte offsets, not backend state.
Core's pool copies the function table once at model load and retains package
leases. Workers use those bound callbacks; scheduling and memory ownership stay
in Core. The independently built DSO initializes its own GGML tables.

## Lifetime and dispatch

SDK 1.2 adds `cpu_backend_abi.h`. `guild_cpu_backend_ext_v2_t` retains the
unchanged CPE1 prefix and appends format-description, canonical planar Q2,
native-Q2 rows, CPU BF16 router and ordered combine callbacks. The canonical
activation image is explicitly 64-byte aligned and 3584 bytes; C and C++ builds
check its frozen layout. Old CPE1 plugins remain readable, but do not supply
the newly appended operations. Core copies and validates only the supported
size-checked prefix before init's stack storage disappears.

The independent CPU 1.1 implementation has oracle tests for the appended
operations, including an AVX2/FMA/F16C canonical-Q2 fallback without VNNI.
Core workers and native-pack format parsing can bind these operations once.
Source ownership transfer and a build without all bundled CPU arithmetic are
separate gates; registering this table alone does not establish either one.

Core owns tensor buffers and scratch; plugins may not retain borrowed pointers
beyond their declared lifetime or free Core allocations. Device launches use
the supplied stream. Models hold the package while bound pointers/graphs exist;
unloading synchronizes work before releasing executable code.

`KernelRegistry::select` and `find_by_id` return `KernelBinding`
(`std::shared_ptr<const guild_kernel_op_desc_v1_t>` aliasing the internal
`StoredOp` and its `library_keepalive`), and `ModelRunnerRegistry` returns
`std::shared_ptr<const IModelRunner>`. Cross-registry publication, enable/disable,
unload, and selection are serialized through `abi::provider_lifecycle_mutex()`,
and `active_package_leases(package_id)` counts both explicit session leases and
live `KernelBinding` / `IModelRunner` references per package. See
[Phase 2E concurrency](PHASE2E_CONCURRENCY.md).
## CUDA execution extensions (SDK 1.4)

`guild/abi/cuda_dense_abi.h` adds the `CDD1` size-checked extension without
changing Kernel ABI v1, PFKE or the frozen seven-pointer prefill table. It carries
BF16/F32 projection, native Q8_1 quantization and native GGUF MMVQ callbacks,
explicit geometry/strides/stream, caller-owned buffer lifetimes, per-call exact
multi-row selection and C status/error records. It exposes no private C++ class
or CUDA SDK type.

`guild/abi/cuda_attn_abi.h` adds the `CDA1` size-checked extension for CUDA
attention, recurrent (GDN), RoPE, KV cache/streaming and QSA selection
operations. It replaces private C++ records (`QsaShapes`, `GdnShapes`,
`QsaAttnPools`, `KvHostPools`, `KvStreamMap`, `QsaIndexerBuffers`, `RopeScaling`)
and process-global native toggles with public C POD descriptors and explicit
configuration callbacks.

`guild/abi/cuda_moe_abi.h` adds the `CDM1` size-checked extension for CUDA MoE
routing/combine/shared/grouped experts, S-family quantized GEMV/dequant,
activation quantization, elementwise/doorbell operations, token sampling,
speculative verify kernels, and an isolated Qwen specialization (`gr`, `fused_gr`,
`ple`, `cvec`). Discovery/registration is not an execution guarantee;
the CUDA ownership document tracks implementation and real-model gates.
